IoT- ja OT-ympäristöjen tietoturva alkaa laitteiden suojaamisesta
items.summary: Lokakuussa 2026 Euroopassa nähtiin laajoja kyberhyökkäyksiä kauppojen kylmäjärjestelmiin. Hyökkääjät pääsivät käsiksi etäohjattaviin laitteisiin ja muuttivat niiden lämpötila- ja sulatusasetuksia. Seurauksena oli elintarvikkeiden pilaantumisia ja merkittäviä taloudellisia vahinkoja. Marraskuun alussa vastaavia hyökkäyksiä raportoitiin jälleen useissa Euroopan maissa, myös Virossa. Vastaavanlaisia epäiltyjä kyberhyökkäyksiä on havaittu nyt myös Suomessa. Tapaukset osoittavat konkreettisesti, kuinka verkkoon yhdistettyjen IoT- ja OT-laitteiden tietoturvapuutteet voivat vaikuttaa suoraan yrityksen toimintaan ja fyysiseen ympäristöön. Internetiin näkyvä, päivittämätön tai puutteellisesti suojattu automaatiolaite voi tarjota hyökkääjälle pääsyn kriittisiin järjestelmiin. Tässä artikkelissa käymme läpi, mitä IoT- ja OT-laitteet ovat, miksi niiden suojaaminen on tärkeää ja millä käytännön toimenpiteillä organisaatiot voivat vähentää niihin kohdistuvia kyberuhkia.

items.title: Fintech platform Sageworks taken offline after suspected cyberattack
items.summary: Financial technology company Abrigo has restored its Sageworks risk management application, except for borrower-facing capabilities, following an outage triggered by "irregular activity" in its environment. On October 30, the company began emergency maintenance and took the Sageworks application offline to investigate suspicious activity detected earlier that day, with the outage continuing through the weekend. Abrigo provides cloud-based software and analytics solutions for community banks and credit unions across the United States. According to the company, it serves more than 2,400 entities.

items.title: Storm Ransomware Is Scaling Fast and Selling an AI Powered Image
items.summary: A new ransomware operation appeared in August 2026 with an ambitious pitch: sophisticated infrastructure, aggressive affiliate payouts, global ambitions, and what it calls the “first AI powered, quantum resistant ransomware.” Within approximately six weeks, Storm had claimed over 50 victims across North America, Europe, and Oceania. Its targets span healthcare, finance, manufacturing, business services, government, transportation, and critical infrastructure. Storm arrived with the structure of an established Ransomware as a Service operation. Its affiliate program offers revenue shares reaching 90%, while its leak site looks closer to a commercial software platform, complete with an interactive victim map, search functionality, sector filters, victim tracking, and document previews.

items.title: Google Disrupts 1.3 Million-Device Android Botnet, Says TV Box Maker Sold Criminal Access
items.summary: A botnet of more than 1.3 million Android devices, mostly TV set-top boxes, lost control of its servers in late October in a takedown led by Google. Google says it is highly confident that device maker Videostrong intentionally put a backdoor in the boxes and sold access to criminals. They used the boxes for ad fraud and to pass other people's internet traffic through owners' home connections. The backdoor is still on the boxes, and owners cannot remove it themselves. Videostrong, based in Shenzhen, China, makes Android TV boxes and other devices under its own name and for other brands. The backdoor, called x.cpe, was built into many device models and brands over several years. Google does not believe a rogue insider or a mistake was to blame. Google used legal action to take down the domains and servers that controlled the botnet. It also took down the control domains of more than a dozen malware families loaded through the backdoor. Japan's National Police Agency, Lumen, HUMAN Security, Plume, Synthient and TrendAI worked with Google on the operation.

items.title: Exploitation Targeting Node-RED, a Tool Embedded in ICS Products
items.summary: On October 30, 2026, one of our canaries caught an attacker exploiting CVE-2026-58115, an unauthenticated Node-RED admin API flaw, to deploy a flow that downloads and runs a Linux bot. The request came from an IP in Microsoft's ASN (AS8075). We have since seen 16 events from the same IP against this CVE, covering several different payloads (see the Update section below). The attacker's request was a complete exploit. It deployed a Node-RED flow, triggered it automatically, and pulled a binary from an attacker-controlled server, all behind three layers of encoding. We decoded each layer and extracted the payload server, the drop path, and the execution method. This post walks through the request, the dropper, and what we can and can't say about the infrastructure behind it. We did not retrieve or analyze the bot binary itself, so we make no claims about its capabilities.

items.title: Russian and Ukrainian hackers hijack emergency apps to spread fake nuclear attack warnings
items.summary: KYIV, Ukraine — Late on Sunday, Kyiv residents received alarming notifications on their phones warning of possible radiation hazard, a chemical threat and ongoing street fighting in the Ukrainian capital. The warnings came from an app that millions of Ukrainians count on as a reliable source of alerts about incoming Russian missiles and drones. But this time, the threats were fake, and the app itself appeared to have been compromised by hackers. Ukraine's Air Force quickly warned that the officially supported Air Alert app had "likely been compromised by the enemy" and urged residents to disregard the messages. A Recorded Future News reporter received several of the notifications, which appeared genuine and even featured the familiar voice used by the app to announce emergencies.

items.title: Critical Langflow Flaws Could Let Unauthenticated Attackers Run Code on Servers
items.summary: Two critical flaws in Langflow could let a remote attacker with no account bypass authentication or run arbitrary code, IBM said last week. Langflow is an open-source tool for building AI agents and workflows, and its vulnerability reports go to IBM. Every release from 1.0.0 through 1.12.8 has the flaws, and the only fix is version 1.13.0. Neither flaw is in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, as of the catalog's October 30 update. Six other Langflow flaws are listed there, most recently CVE-2026-9198, which was added in August.

items.title: Government Linux Servers Targeted With SysGoRAT and Suspected AI-Generated Scripts
items.summary: Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of a cyber espionage campaign specifically targeting Linux infrastructure associated with government entities and state-affiliated infrastructure. The activity, observed by Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 between October 2025 and April 2026, has been tracked under the moniker CL-UNK-1211, where "CL" refers to cluster and "UNK" stands for unknown motivation. A notable aspect of the campaign concerns the use of large language models (LLMs) and/or automated artificial intelligence (AI) agents to generate payloads and execute malicious code. "The attackers behind this cluster of activity focused on Linux environments to conduct extensive reconnaissance and maintain persistent network access to support intelligence-gathering," researchers Roey Porat and Tom Fakterman said. "The attackers attempted to dump sensitive databases and exfiltrate government mailboxes to access social media accounts." The campaign employs a "versatile operational playbook," leveraging a combination of open-source tools, custom cross-platform backdoors, and web shells to maintain access. Another hallmark involves attempts to disable endpoint protections, wipe system logs, and plant deceptive red-team markers so as to disguise the activity as a legitimate security assessment.

items.title: New VOLTA Infostealer Uses Claude, Gemini, and Kimi AI to Rank Victims by Financial Value
items.summary: Cybersecurity researchers have discovered a new Windows infostealer malware called VOLTA-AUTODOXER (aka VOLTA) that makes use of a large language model (LLM) to rank a victim's stolen data by their monetization value. Like other typical stealer families, VOLTA is equipped to harvest passwords and cookies from Chromium-based web browsers; data from Outlook profiles and Slack workspaces; payment cards; cryptocurrency wallet seed phrases; Discord, Telegram, Steam, and Roblox sessions; Microsoft OAuth tokens; SSH and cloud-provider keys; Wi-Fi profiles; and screenshots. "VOLTA builds a structured evidence bundle about the person behind the machine," Cisco Talos researcher Ryan Fetterman said. "This bundle contains geolocation and home address, employer and employer domain, inferred birth year, card last-4 digits, Slack workspaces, document authorship metadata, iPhone backup indicators, and a live Roblox account valuation." To make this information more valuable, the malware uses stolen session access to search the victim's Gmail account for receipts to corroborate the home address by extracting emails related to Amazon, DoorDash, Uber Eats, Grubhub, Walmart, and PayPal.

items.title: Vulnerabilities in Eclipse ThreadX
items.summary: Classification: Severe, Solution: Official Fix, Exploit Maturity: Not Defined, CVSSv3.1: 8.7, CVEs: CVE-2026-114408, CVE-2026-115654, CVE-2026-115653, Summary: CVE-2026-114408 (CVSS: 8.7): _nx_icmpv6_process_packet_too_big adds the destination quoted in an ICMPv6 Packet Too Big message to the destination table, then reads the entry the add returns without checking that the add succeeded. When the table is full, the add fails and returns a NULL entry, and the function dereferences it. A sender that fills the table with Packet Too Big messages quoting new destinations crashes the IP thread with the next one. CVE-2026-115654 (CVSS: 6.9): A user-mode, memory-protected module can suspend, resume, terminate, reset or re-prioritise threads it does not own, and abort their waits. The Module Manager's thread-control dispatchers only establish that the pointer a module passes names a live thread outside the module; they do not check that the thread belongs to the calling module. Every application thread and every other module's thread is therefore under the control of any loaded module, which can stop them permanently or change how the system schedules them. CVE-2026-115653 (CVSS: 7.0): On the Cortex-M module ports, the PendSV handler saves a preempted thread's callee-saved registers and its exception-return value in privileged mode, at addresses taken from the thread's process stack pointer, without checking that pointer against the thread's stack. A user-mode, memory-protected module that points its stack pointer just above the start of any region it may write has up to nine words — 25 with the floating-point unit — written in privileged mode into the memory immediately below that region, eight of them with values it chose, and reads back what is there when the thread is next switched in. See also: https://github.com/eclipse-threadx/threadx/security/advisories/GHSA-5q6x-rxf3-5q5f, See also: https://github.com/eclipse-threadx/threadx/security/advisories/GHSA-c38r-v552-gh5g

items.title: Hackers disrupt refrigeration systems at European supermarkets
items.summary: A cyberattack on refrigeration systems has disrupted stores run by multiple supermarket chains across several European countries after hackers remotely changed temperature settings on freezers and cooling systems. In some cases, hackers shut down refrigerators or activated defrosting systems, causing temperatures to rise, resulting in significant product losses and forcing store managers to intervene early in the morning. Refrigeration failures were identified at dozens of supermarkets, but it is unclear whether they were hit in a coordinated attack or targeted individually.

items.title: Vulnerabilities in Control Web Panel
items.summary: Classification: Severe, Solution: Official Fix, Exploit Maturity: Not Defined, CVSSv4.0: 9.3, CVEs: CVE-2026-77877, CVE-2026-77878, CVE-2026-77879, CVE-2026-77880, CVE-2026-104080, CVE-2026-77876, CVE-2026-73695, CVE-2026-73696, CVE-2026-73697, Summary: CVE-2026-77877 (CVSS: 8.6): Control Web Panel (CWP) before webpanel_version 1.30 contains a missing authentication vulnerability that allows attackers able to reach the loopback API service to invoke root-privileged API routes without presenting an access token. Attackers can access endpoints such as /v1/restoredatabase/, /generaluser/, /last_access/, /valid_user/, /valid_token/, and /user_panel_dashboard/ to perform unauthorized actions with root privileges. CVE-2026-77878 (CVSS: 8.6): Control Web Panel (CWP) before webpanel_version 1.30 contains an OS command injection vulnerability in the loopback API database restore route /v1/restoredatabase/, where the restoreDBBackup() handler passes an attacker-controlled file path from the POST body into a shell command without proper escaping. An attacker able to reach the route can inject arbitrary OS commands that execute as root. CVE-2026-77879 (CVSS: 8.6): Control Web Panel (CWP) before webpanel_version 1.16 contains a SQL injection vulnerability in the loopback API authentication gate access_token(), which connects to MySQL as root and interpolates attacker-controlled values directly into its query. Attackers can inject SQL through the authorization_code and client_id parameters to read arbitrary database contents and forge the authentication result, bypassing the API's authentication check. CVE-2026-77880 (CVSS: 8.6): Control Web Panel (CWP) before webpanel_version 1.16 contains an OS command injection vulnerability in the loopback API password change route /newpass/, which runs as root. An attacker can inject arbitrary OS commands by manipulating the POST 'user' parameter that is passed unescaped into a shell command, achieving remote code execution with root privileges. CVE-2026-104080 (CVSS: 8.6): Control Web Panel (CWP) before webpanel_version 1.30 contains an OS command injection vulnerability in the loopback API /valid_token/ route that allows unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary commands as root by injecting shell metacharacters into the unvalidated 'user' parameter. Attackers can send a crafted request to the /valid_token/ route, which passes the parameter unescaped into a shell_exec() call. CVE-2026-77876 (CVSS: 9.3): Control Web Panel (CWP) before webpanel_version 1.16 contains an OS command injection vulnerability in the protected_directory user panel module that allows attackers to execute arbitrary commands by submitting unescaped input through the file POST parameter in the acc=deletedp action. Attackers can exploit this flaw, which passes attacker-controlled input directly into a shell_exec call, to achieve code execution in the user panel context. items.title: Over 1,000 GitLab servers vulnerable to ongoing RCE attacks
items.summary: Over 1,000 Internet-exposed GitLab servers are still unpatched against a maximum-severity flaw actively exploited in remote code execution attacks. Tracked as CVE-2026-97229, this vulnerability stems from an integer overflow weakness and was discovered in the CI/CD Regular Expression Compiler, which parses and evaluates regular expressions in pipeline configuration files. "GitLab has remediated an issue that, under certain conditions, could have allowed an unauthenticated user to execute arbitrary code on the GitLab server via a specially crafted regular expression in a CI/CD configuration, due to insufficient regular expression validation," the company explained on October 12 when it released security patches to address the security issue in GitLab Community Edition (CE) and Enterprise Edition (EE) versions 19.4.2, 19.3.5, and 19.2.8.

items.title: Critical Vulnerability in Linux kernel's IPv4 networking subsystem
items.summary: Classification: Critical, Solution: Official Fix, Exploit Maturity: Not Defined, CVSSv3.1: 9.8, CVEs: CVE-2026-98432, Summary: A use-after-free vulnerability was found in the Linux kernel's IPv4 networking subsystem. A remote, unauthenticated attacker could exploit a race condition during TCP connection request processing to trigger remote code execution. The flaw arises when socket options are freed while still being accessed by a concurrent operation, such as a retransmitted connection request or a socket migration. Exploitation requires precise timing of network requests but does not require any privileges or user interaction. This vulnerability affects any system running a vulnerable kernel version with IPv4 TCP networking enabled. Since TCP is fundamental to nearly all networked services, the affected surface is broad. Systems accepting inbound TCP connections are most directly exposed. The investigation is ongoing and this bulletin will be updated as new information emerges. Log in with your Red Hat account, then click the "Follow" button below to be notified of changes to this bulletin.

items.title: Synology warns of C3RB3R ransomware attacks targeting NAS devices
items.summary: Taiwanese network-attached storage (NAS) appliance maker Synology warned customers to update their devices immediately due to a surge in C3RB3r ransomware attacks. The company urged users to enable automatic updates and upgrade the DiskStation Manager (DSM) software running on their NAS devices to the latest version to protect their data. "Synology has identified threat actors exploiting a vulnerability patched in December 2024 to target devices running outdated versions of DSM. These attacks aim to encrypt data and extort ransom," it said in a Thursday advisory.

items.summary: The newly patched bugs are CVE-2026-111357 and CVE-2026-118527. Ivanti added them on Thursday to its October 13 advisory describing CVE-2026-104935, an authentication bypass in the VPN product. According to Ivanti, attacks chaining the three flaws had hit a limited number of customers by the time they were disclosed. CVE-2026-111357, which Ivanti rates 8.8 on the CVSS scale, stems from the lack of authentication for a critical function. It enables an authenticated attacker with local access to elevate their privileges. This is the privilege escalation zero-day for which no fix was available when the attacks came to light in mid-October. CVE-2026-118527, with a CVSS score of 4.3, involves the generation of predictable identifiers. items.title: The Rise of LLMJacking: How Threat Actors Monetize Compromised Cloud and Model Resources
items.summary: Mandiant responded to multiple incidents in 2026 in which threat actors hijacked enterprise access to Large Language Models (LLMs), a tactic known as "LLMJacking." Spanning a variety of cloud and LLM providers, these intrusions impacted organizations in North America, South America, and Asia Pacific across the financial services, retail, technology, and transportation sectors. Unlike the gradual resource consumption associated with cryptojacking, LLMJacking can generate large spikes in fraudulent cloud charges in a matter of hours. Across individual incidents, we observed fraudulent charges associated with resource consumption exceeding $100,000 USD in a single day, with cumulative charges at some organizations reaching $1 million USD before access was revoked.

items.title: Shutting the Door on the XCPE Botnet
items.summary: Last week, Google and industry partners dismantled the XCPE backdoor which enrolled more than 1.3 million set-top boxes into a botnet. We assess with high confidence that the backdoor and botnet were intentionally developed, deployed, and operated for financial gain by Videostrong Technology Co., an Android Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) and Original Design Manufacturer (ODM). Videostrong monetized the backdoor by selling access to criminal affiliates and loading those affiliates’ malware modules onto infected devices. These secondary modules were conducting ad-fraud; silently enrolling infected devices into residential proxy networks; and loading additional malware onto XCPE-compromised devices. We also took action to disrupt the command and control (C2) domains that operate these affiliate modules. Because these affiliates each have diversified distribution channels for their modules beyond XCPE, we assess that taking down their C2 domains will sever access to at least 10 million additional compromised devices. We found this malicious software built directly into many different device models and brands over multiple years, supported by dedicated infrastructure and constantly evolving configurations to evade detection and manage their affiliates. We believe this campaign wasn’t an isolated rogue insider or a development oversight. As a result, Google has cut ties with Videostrong and banned them from making devices with preloaded Google apps.

items.title: BITTER Expands Its Arsenal with PapRAT
items.summary: BITTER is a suspected South Asian cyberespionage group active since at least 2013, with a history of targeting the government, energy, and engineering sectors. Over the past several months, FortiGuard Labs has tracked a campaign targeting South Asian organizations that uses PowerShell scripts and a custom remote access trojan (RAT), which we call PapRAT, to establish persistent access to victim environments. Based on lure filenames, command-and-control (C2) communication patterns, file metadata, and malware analysis, we attribute this activity to BITTER with high confidence. The campaign uses three distinct infection chains. The first uses a malicious LNK file that abuses the native Windows ftp.exe utility to execute scripts and create scheduled tasks that maintain contact with the attacker’s C2 server. The second uses a VHDX disk image containing a LNK file that opens a decoy spreadsheet while silently launching an MSI installer to deploy PapRAT. The third begins with a URL shortcut that retrieves a LNK file through WebDAV, leading to an MSI installer that deploys PapRAT. In this chain, PapRAT also delivers WmRAT, a secondary implant previously documented by other researchers.
